items.title: Lake Bellaire
items.html:
Just 1.5 Miles to Lake Bellaire

Discover this local treasure—a peaceful, scenic lake perfect for fishing, paddling, wildlife viewing, or a lakeside picnic.

Getting There & Amenities:
• Fisherman’s Paradise (DNR Access): Developed boat ramp, dock, parking, and pit-toilet restrooms. A Michigan Recreation Passport is required; posted launch/parking fees (about $11–12) may also apply. Michigan Water Trails
• Cottage Drive Family Park (Miley’s Beach): On the western shore, with a sandy swimming beach, picnic tables, grills, and restrooms. Forest Home Township Parks

What You Might Catch: Trout, bass, walleye, pike, lake trout—plus birdwatching and peaceful water views. Watershed Council

Local Stewardship: The Three Lakes Association supports and conserves Lake Bellaire’s natural beauty—great for those interested in eco-friendly tourism. Three Lakes Association

Feel free to ask for help with maps, kayak or boat rental options, or the best times to fish!

items.title: Torch Lake
items.html:
📍 Torch Lake Info (Tip of the Mitt Watershed Council)

Just a short drive from your stay, Torch Lake offers legendary turquoise waters and world-class fishing opportunities. From casting for bass and perch in shallow bays to trolling deep for lake trout or salmon, this lake is an angler’s dream.

• What You Can Catch: Trout, bass, pike, salmon, perch & more
• Best Spots: Drop-offs, rocky points, and deeper waters
• Access Points: Torch Lake Township Day Park, Torch River Bridge DNR launch
• Need Help? Local fishing charters are available for guided adventures

Fishing Highlights

Torch Lake is a premier destination for fishing enthusiasts of all levels:

  • Lake Trout – thrive in the cold, deep waters.
  • Atlantic Salmon, Steelhead & Brown Trout – targeted by local trolling charters.
  • Smallmouth Bass – plentiful along rocky points and weed beds.
  • Northern Pike & Muskellunge – trophy-sized catches possible.
  • Yellow Perch – jumbo perch school up in the fall; great for families.

For guided fishing trips, check out local charters such as:

  • Charters North – Captain Shaun (231-590-1949)
  • Fish With Jim Outfitters (248-252-1277)

items.html:
Website: https://watershedcouncil.org/waterbody/clam-lake/
Location: Between Torch Lake and Lake Bellaire

A long, slender connecting lake on the Chain of Lakes, Clam Lake offers good fishing for panfish, perch, and bass. The Grass River flows in from Lake Bellaire at the east end—a popular fishing spot—and the short Clam River carries the water out to Torch Lake. Because it’s smaller and calmer than the big lakes, it’s ideal for kayaks and smaller boats.

items.title: Schuss Mountain Trail Map
items.html:
Welcome to one of Michigan’s top ski destinations—where terrain, trails, and fun come together at Schuss Mountain, Shanty Creek Resort.

Trail Overview
Schuss Mountain has about 42 trails for every skill level, plus 2 terrain parks and 7 lifts. All downhill skiing at Shanty Creek is at Schuss Mountain (Summit Mountain is home to Alpine Tubing).

Trail Difficulty
● Green Circle – Easiest: wide, gentle slopes for beginners
■ Blue Square – More Difficult: for developing skiers
◆ Black Diamond – Most Difficult: steeper, faster terrain

Lifts

  • Quad chairlifts – color-named (Red, Yellow, Purple and more) serving the front face and north side
  • Magic carpet and handle tow – for beginners, ski school and the Low Rider park

Terrain Parks

  • Mellow Yellow – the main park, with big boxes, rails and jumps
  • Low Rider – smaller features near the Yellow Lift, served by a handle tow; great for building confidence

Key Areas

  • Schuss Village – Base area with day lodge, rentals, tickets, ski school, and food
  • Cedar River Village – Lodging at the top of the mountain
  • Ski Patrol – On the mountain for safety and assistance

2026–27 Season (projected): Dec 5, 2026 – Mar 22, 2027
Hours: Sun 9am–4:30pm; Mon–Tue 10am–4:30pm; Wed–Sat and holidays 9am–9pm once night skiing begins.

Tips for Visitors

  • Start your day early for fresh corduroy runs
  • Green trails near the base are best for families and beginners
  • Use lift maps and signage to plan your route across the mountain
  • Helmets are recommended for all riders

Download full trail map: Schuss Mountain Trail Map PDF

If skiing and snowboarding aren’t your thing—don’t worry! There’s still a fast and fun way to enjoy the snow. Alpine Tubing at Summit Mountain is a must-try winter activity, delivering all the thrills of sledding without the uphill climb.

items.title: Grass River Nature Area Tours
items.html:
Kayak Tours

https://www.grassriver.org/river-tours.html

items.title: Torch Lake Sandbar
items.html:
A Must-Visit Gem Near Bellaire, MI

More info: torchlake.com
Location: South end of Torch Lake near the Torch River (Rapid City / Alden area); reached by boat from Bellaire via Lake Bellaire, Clam Lake and Torch Lake

Access: Best reached by boat, kayak, or jet ski; rentals available nearby

Torch Lake Sandbar is famous for its stunning, crystal-clear turquoise waters and soft sandy bottom. Perfect for swimming, sunbathing, and boating, it's a must-visit spot for a relaxing day on the water. Bring your snacks and sunscreen, and enjoy this beautiful natural gem!

FAQs – What Guests Should Know

  • How do I get there?
    You'll need a boat or watercraft—rent from a nearby marina or charter a cruise with a captain for a no-hassle trip.
  • Can we swim at the sandbar?
    Yes! The water is shallow and perfect for swimming and wading.
  • Can we bring drinks and snacks?
    Absolutely! Picnic-friendly—just be respectful and take your trash with you.
  • Is it a party spot or family-friendly?
    It can be both! Weekends (especially the Fourth of July) bring a lively crowd, while weekdays are more relaxed.
  • When's the best time to go?
    Arrive early in the day for calmer waters and easy anchoring—especially on weekends and holidays.

Whether you're seeking a quiet escape or an adventure in nature, Antrim Creek Natural Area & Rex Beach offers a perfect blend of outdoor recreation and natural beauty, just a short drive from Bellaire.

items.title: Grass River Natural Area — Kayaking & Nature Escape
items.html:
Website: https://www.grassriver.org/
Phone: (231) 533-8576 (Grass River Center)
Location Guide: 6500 Alden Hwy, Bellaire, MI 49615 - About 10 minutes' drive from downtown Bellaire
Hours: Trails open daily, dawn to dusk; Grass River Center open daily 10 a.m.–4 p.m. May–October (weekends Nov–Apr)

Immerse yourself in nature at Grass River Natural Area, a 1,500-acre preserve perfect for kayaking and wildlife viewing. Paddle the calm Grass River framed by forests and wetlands and spot local wildlife in their natural habitat. Kayak rentals are available seasonally, letting you explore on your own, or join a guided kayak tour to learn about the area's rich ecology.

Guest Tips:

  • Kayak rentals are available June through September and must be reserved in advance by phone.
  • Rentals run during Center hours (10 AM–4 PM) and leave from the Grass River Overlook; kayaks must be back by 4 PM. About $30 for 2–3 hours or $50 for 4–6 hours.
  • Only six single kayaks (no tandems), for adults and teens only.
  • Wear comfortable, water-friendly footwear and bring insect repellent.
  • Don't miss the boardwalk trails—dogs are allowed on-leash only on the Rail and Algonquin trails, not the boardwalks.

Cruise the beautiful Torch, Clam, and Lake Bellaire aboard a pontoon or tritoon boat. Bellaire Pontoon Boat Rental shares its phone and fleet with Northaire Resort & Pontoon Rentals, with private docks in Bellaire, on Clam Lake and on Torch Lake, and a safety boat on call for peace of mind. Want someone else to drive? Book the captained 2-hour sunset cruise on Torch Lake. Enjoy a stress-free day on the water, perfect for families, friends, or special occasions.

FAQs

  • Are captains provided for rentals?
    Rentals are self-drive; a licensed captain is included on the sunset cruise.
  • What are the rental hours?
    Boat pick-up from 9 a.m., return by 7 p.m.
  • Where do I pick up the boat?
    At the Bellaire dock (or the Clam Lake/Torch Lake docks)—your location is confirmed before your trip.
  • Is there a safety boat on standby?
    Yes, a safety boat is on call.
  • Can the rental accommodate special occasions like parties?
    Absolutely! Perfect for family outings and celebrations.

items.title: Dockside Water Sports
items.html:
Website: https://www.dockside-watersports.com/
Phone: 231-377-7777 ext. 2
Location: 6326 Old Torch Lake Dr, Bellaire, MI 49615 — right on Torch Lake next to Dockside Restaurant
Season: Late May to mid-September, daily 9:30 a.m.–7:30 p.m., weather permitting (2026 dates: May 23–Sept 13)

Ready for high-performance fun on Northern Michigan's clearest waters? Dockside Water Sports offers luxury pontoon/tritoon rentals and thrilling jet skis, perfect for both laid-back lake cruising and adrenaline-pumping rides. As the only rental company right on Torch Lake's open shoreline, you can head straight out—and come back anytime for restrooms, snacks, lunch at Dockside Restaurant, or a rest at the beach. Whether you're seeking family-friendly fun or fast-paced adventure, this is your launchpad to unforgettable lake memories.

FAQs

  • Are captains available for boat rentals?
    Rentals are self-operated; staff give a full tutorial and can take you out for a hands-on demo if needed.
  • Is beach access included?
    Yes, you can return to the Dockside home base and beach during your rental.
  • What amenities are available on-site?
    Valet docking, restrooms, the Dockside Restaurant, and staff who carry your gear and fill your cooler with ice.
  • Can we bring food and drinks onboard?
    Yes! Coolers and snacks are welcome—just pack responsibly.
  • Is training provided for first-time jet ski or boat users?
    Absolutely. Staff provide safety and operating instructions before departure.

items.title: Foxy’s Custom Cruises (“Ahoy Matey!”)
items.html:
Website: https://www.foxyscustomcruises.com

Phone: (231) 944-6823 (text Capt. Foxy for dates, times and payment)
Dock: Clam River Marina, 6349 Old Torch Lake Dr, Bellaire, MI 49615 — dock #22 (follow signs to Dockside Restaurant, turn through the 'Clam River Marina' gate; don't park in Dockside's lot)

Hop aboard with Foxy's Custom Cruises, captained by Capt. Foxy—a Coast Guard–certified captain with 20+ years on Torch Lake—and Capt. Rob, a retired Air Force veteran and self-described 'sandbar guy.' Foxy's offers the perfect mix of adventure, celebration, and lake-life fun on Torch Lake. Choose from the Sandbar Splash Day, Sunday Funday, Torch Lake Tour, Fun in the Sun, or a Bachelorette Party cruise, or ask about a custom cruise.

FAQs

  • How many people can come?
    Up to 6 passengers per cruise, with up to 4 more at an extra per-person fee (10 max).
  • Are the cruises family-friendly?
    Yes—bring your own life jackets for children 3 and under.
  • Can we bring drinks or food onboard?
    Yes, coolers and snacks are welcome. Tips are appreciated!
  • What kind of events are best for Foxy's?
    Bachelorette parties, birthdays, family outings, or just relaxing with friends at the sandbar.
  • Do we need boating experience?
    Not at all—your captain handles everything so you can kick back and enjoy the ride.

items.title: M‑88 Boat & Dock Rentals
items.html:
Website: https://www.m88boatrentals.com/

Phone: (231) 320-0190
Location: 100 Ohio St, Bellaire, MI 49615 — Right on the Intermediate River, downtown Bellaire
Hours: Mon–Fri 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; Sat–Sun 10 a.m.–4 p.m.

Note: No boat rentals in 2026 — dock rentals only. Pontoon rentals are expected to return in summer 2027.

M-88 Boat & Dock Rentals offers daily, weekly and seasonal dock slips in downtown Bellaire on the Intermediate River, with easy access to Lake Bellaire, the Grass River, Clam Lake and Torch Lake. When pontoon rentals return, boats are docked in the water—just park in the public lot by the village boat launch, meet them at the shed at 100 Ohio Street, and step aboard. No trailers or ramps needed!

Guest Tips:

  • Bringing your own boat? Reserve a daily or weekly dock online.
  • Pontoon rentals (when offered) run daily or multi-day; boats must be returned with a full tank.
  • They keep a limited supply of comfortable infant, child and youth life jackets on request—Michigan law requires children under 6 to wear one while underway.
  • Full refund for boat-rental cancellations made 48 hours in advance.

items.title: Northaire Resort & Pontoon Rentals
items.html:
Website: https://www.northaireresort.com/
Phone: (231) 377-7764
Location Guide: 7067 Crystal Springs Rd, Bellaire, MI 49615 — on the south shore of Clam Lake, about 15 minutes' drive from downtown Bellaire (additional docks on Torch Lake and in Bellaire)

Set sail from a classic Up North destination with the largest fleet of pontoons on Torch Lake, Clam Lake and Lake Bellaire! Northaire Resort has been making lake dreams come true since 1948. With private docks at the resort on Clam Lake, on Torch Lake, and in Bellaire, it's the ideal launch point for everything from tranquil morning cruises to tubing afternoons and golden-hour sunset rides.

Their boats come with Bluetooth stereo, GPS depth finder, bimini top, ladder, changing room and a tow bar for tubing. Tubes, lily pads and porta-potties are available to add on, and jet skis rent from the Torch Lake location. Whether you're celebrating something big or just living your best lake life, Northaire makes it seamless and stress-free.

FAQs

  • Are captains available?
    Yes, on the captained 2-hour Torch Lake sunset cruise; ask about other options when booking.
  • Where do we pick up the boat?
    At one of Northaire's three private docks (resort, Torch Lake, or Bellaire)—not public ramps. Confirm your dock before heading out.
  • Can we bring our own food and drinks?
    Absolutely—coolers, snacks, and beverages are welcome on board.
  • What are the rental hours?
    Pick-up begins at 9 AM and boats are due back by 7 PM; early pick-up is available for an hourly fee.
  • How far is it to the Torch Lake Sandbar?
    The sandbar is at the south end of Torch Lake; from Clam Lake you'll head out the Clam River into Torch Lake and cruise south.

items.title: Torch Lake Sunset Cruises
items.html:
Website: https://www.northaireresort.com/sunset-cruises
Phone: (231) 377-7764
Location: Departs from the Clam River right by Dockside Restaurant, Old Torch Lake Dr, Bellaire, MI
Tour Duration: 2 hours
Price: $75 per person (2-person minimum)
Captain Provided: Yes – licensed captain included

Treat yourself to a magical evening on Torch Lake with a 2-hour, captained sunset cruise run by Northaire Resort. Your captain will take you from the Clam River out to Torch Lake's stunning blue expanse as the sun dips into the horizon. Bring your own beverages and snacks—a cooler full of ice is provided.

Perfect for couples, families, or small groups, this stress-free experience is all about unwinding and soaking in one of the most beautiful sunsets in the Midwest. No boating experience needed—just show up and enjoy!

FAQs

  • Do we need boating experience?
    Not at all! A licensed captain does all the driving—just relax and enjoy.
  • Can we bring drinks and snacks?
    Yes! Bring your favorites—a cooler full of ice is provided.
  • How long is the cruise?
    About 2 hours; the start time depends on sunset and is set when you book.
  • Where do we board the boat?
    On the Clam River right by Dockside Restaurant, near Torch Lake.
  • Is this good for groups?
    Yes! It's ideal for couples, families, or small parties looking to unwind together.

items.title: Vacation Water Sports
items.html:
Website: https://www.vacationwatersports.com/
Phone: (231) 350-8745

Delivery-based — serving Torch Lake (Alden), Clam Lake, Lake Bellaire, Intermediate Lake (Central Lake) & Elk Lake (Elk Rapids)
Season: Mid-May through late September (2026: May 15–Sept 27)

Experience lake freedom with Vacation Water Sports—a rental outfitter that delivers jet skis and pontoons to drop-off locations around the Chain of Lakes, so you can start your adventure without towing a thing. Whether you're chasing thrills on a jet ski or cruising Lake Bellaire and Torch Lake in comfort, their daily and multi-day rentals make boat days effortless and fun.

FAQs

  • Will they deliver near our rental?
    They deliver to set drop-off locations on the lakes they serve; other locations may be available on request (extra charge may apply)—call to arrange.
  • Can we rent for multiple days?
    Yes—1 to 10 day rentals; a 3-day minimum applies July 3–Aug 16 (holiday rates; no refunds for 4th of July week).
  • What lakes do they service?
    Torch Lake, Clam Lake, Lake Bellaire, Intermediate Lake & Elk Lake.
  • How long is a one-day rental?
    8 hours. Tubes for pontoons are free; fuel is charged at marina rates.
  • Any rules to know?
    No pets, and boat capacity limits are strictly enforced. Waivers are completed online for each driver/rider.

items.title: Swimming Pools at Shanty Creek
items.html:
Whether you're cooling off in summer or relaxing after a day on the slopes, Shanty Creek has pools across its villages.

  • The Lakeview Hotel (Summit Village) – indoor pool (open daily 9am–11pm) and a seasonal outdoor pool (summer only).
  • The Lodge at Cedar River – heated outdoor pool and hot tubs, reserved for Cedar River lodging guests and property owners.

Your pool pass covers the Lakeview Hotel indoor and outdoor pools only. The other village pools are not included with your stay.

The resort only provides pool towels to its own lodging guests, so please bring the towel basket we provide with your pool pass.

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/stay/fitness-center/

items.title: Children’s Play Area – Summit Village
items.html:
Fun for the little ones (and a peaceful break for you!)
Located near The Lakeview Hotel and Summit Fitness Center, the Summit Village children’s playground offers a welcome spot for kids to let off energy while parents relax.

What to Expect:

  • Nature-inspired play equipment including slides, climbing structures, and open space
  • Shaded areas perfect for little explorers
  • Close to amenities like restrooms, dining, and the fitness center
  • Ideal for combined family time—kids can play while you plan your next adventure

This playground is especially handy when visiting the Lodge or staying in Summit Village lodging.

items.title: Tennis at Summit Village
items.html:
Serve up summer fun with a game of tennis at Shanty Creek! Located in Summit Village, the tennis courts offer scenic views overlooking the golf course—making each match both competitive and picturesque.

Racquets and tennis balls are available for use from the Summit Fitness Center, so you can hit the court without packing gear.

Whether you're a seasoned player or just looking for a friendly rally, the courts at Shanty Creek are a great way to stay active and soak up the northern Michigan sunshine.

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/stay/more-fun-in-the-sun/

items.title: Disc Golf at Summit Golf Club
items.html:
Get outside and enjoy a fun, casual round on Shanty Creek’s 9-hole Disc Golf & Foot Golf course at Summit Golf Club in Summit Village.

Perfect for families, beginners, or seasoned disc golfers looking for a relaxed round with a view. It’s a great way to enjoy the outdoors while getting in some light activity.

Discs, scorecards, and course maps are available at the Summit/Legend Pro Shop. $12 includes a disc. To make a tee time, call 231-533-2020.

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/golf/golf-2-0/#footgolf

items.title: Go Outside and Play
items.html:
Unplug, unwind, and get active with a variety of outdoor games around the resort. Whether you’re looking for a friendly match or a spontaneous showdown, there’s something for everyone.

Try your hand at:
• A quick game of H-O-R-S-E on the basketball court
• Sand volleyball under the summer sun
• A match of badminton or shuffleboard
• Laid-back fun with bocce ball, tetherball, or wiffle ball
• Or hit the tennis courts for something more competitive

Most equipment is available on-site—just show up and play!

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/stay/more-fun-in-the-sun/

items.title: Lawn Games
items.html:
Let’s Play! Summer days at Shanty Creek are perfect for some classic fun on the lawn.

Challenge friends and family with traditional favorites and supersized fun:

• Horseshoes
• Croquet
• Bean Bag Toss
• Ladder Ball
• Washer Toss
• Giant Checkers
• Giant Jenga
• Giant Dominos
• Lawn Yahtzee

For game info and equipment, stop by the Summit Fitness Center in Summit Village. Let the games begin!

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/stay/more-fun-in-the-sun/

items.title: Boating
items.html:
There’s nothing like being on the water—and Antrim County’s Chain of Lakes delivers it all.

Whether you're:
• Splashing on the sandbar with friends
• Water skiing or wakeboarding
• Kayaking or paddling down peaceful rivers
• Fishing for bass and walleye

This 75-mile waterway system connects lakes and rivers perfect for boating adventures, relaxation, and fun in the sun.

Bring your own boat or rent locally—just get out there and enjoy northern Michigan’s freshwater paradise!

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/stay/more-fun-in-the-sun/

items.title: Biking
items.html:
Antrim County is a cyclist’s dream, whether you prefer the road or rugged trails.

  • Road Biking: Ride the quiet, rolling hills and scenic byways with minimal traffic and stunning views.
  • Mountain Biking: Explore Glacial Hills, one of Michigan’s premier trail systems with loops for all skill levels.
  • E-Bike Rentals (summer season): New to biking or want help with the hills? Rent a motor-assisted e-bike from the Summit Fitness Center: 6 hours $65, 12 hours $132. Pick-up 9am–5pm; call 231-533-7060.
  • Traditional Bikes are also available for cruising around the resort.

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/stay/fitness-center/

items.title: Hiking
items.html:
Looking for a scenic workout? Shanty Creek offers hiking experiences for every pace and preference:

  • Schuss Mountain Trails – Tackle a summertime climb for a rewarding hike with panoramic views of northern Michigan.
  • Grass River Natural Area – Just a short drive away, this network of trails winds through forests, wetlands, and along the water’s edge. It's perfect for peaceful nature walks and wildlife spotting.

Whether you're in it for fitness or fresh air, these trails highlight the natural beauty of the region.

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/stay/more-fun-in-the-sun/

items.title: After Dark | Outdoor Movies + Stargazing
items.html:
When the sun goes down, the fun doesn’t stop at Shanty Creek.

Outdoor Movies on the Mountain
On select summer Saturday nights, the resort has hosted family-friendly outdoor movies atop Summit Mountain. Check the events calendar or ask the front desk for upcoming dates.

Stargazing in Northern Michigan
Clear skies bring out a whole new show: the stars. Far from city lights, Shanty Creek is a great place to spot constellations, shooting stars, and if you're lucky, the Northern Lights.

Tip: Dress warm and bring a thermos. Even summer nights can get cool at the top.

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/stay/more-fun-in-the-sun/

items.title: Schuss Mountain Trail Map
items.html:
Welcome to Schuss Mountain at Shanty Creek Resort, where terrain, trails, and fun come together.

Schuss Mountain has about 42 trails for all skill levels, with groomed runs, glades, two terrain parks, and great views across the mountain.

Trail difficulty

  • ● Green circle – Easiest: wide, gentle slopes for beginners
  • ■ Blue square – More difficult: for developing skiers
  • ◆ Black diamond – Most difficult: steeper, faster terrain and glades

Lifts

  • Five chairlifts – Pink, Blue, Yellow, Purple, and Red
  • Purple Lift – Rises from Cedar River Village for ski-in/ski-out access
  • Red Lift – Serves the back side of the mountain
  • Surface lifts – Magic carpet and handle tow for beginners and the small terrain park

Terrain parks

  • Mellow Yellow – The main park: big boxes, rails, and jumps
  • Low Rider – A smaller, handle-tow park near the Yellow Lift for building confidence

Key areas

  • Schuss Village – Base area with day lodge, tickets, rentals, ski school, and Ivan’s
  • Cedar River Village – Ski-in/ski-out lodging next to the Purple Lift

Tips for Visitors

  • Start your day early for fresh corduroy runs
  • Green trails near the base are best for families and beginners
  • Use lift maps and signage to plan your route across the mountain
  • Helmets are recommended for all riders

Trail map: Schuss Mountain Trail Map

items.title: Nordic Trail Map
items.html:
Explore the snow-covered beauty of Shanty Creek Resort on its scenic Nordic ski and snowshoe trails. Whether you're a beginner or an experienced skier, these trails offer a peaceful and invigorating way to enjoy winter.

Trail overview (2026 map)

  • Pine Cone – 4.5 km, Schuss Village
  • Winter Brook – 1.5 km, Schuss Village
  • Arnie’s Way – 1 km, Summit Village
  • Summit Loop – 1 km, Summit Village
  • Multi-purpose trail – 3 km groomed trail at Schuss Village for snowshoeing and fat tire biking

Trails are marked by difficulty (easiest, moderate, difficult) with trailhead signs. Landmarks along the way include Red Lift Corner, Riverview, and #3 Tee.

Nordic Center hours (2026–27 season, projected Dec 26 – Mar 13):

  • Thu & Mon: 9am – 4pm
  • Fri: 10am – 4pm
  • Sat, Sun & holidays: 9am – 5pm
  • Closed: Tue & Wed

View the trail map: 2026 Nordic Trail Map

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/ski/nordic-trails/

items.title: Skiing & Snowboarding
items.html:
Shanty Creek Resort is one of Michigan’s most beloved ski destinations. Schuss Mountain has about 42 downhill trails, five chairlifts, and two terrain parks, making it ideal for skiers and snowboarders of all skill levels. Alpine tubing is next door at Summit Mountain.

Whether you’re a beginner looking for gentle runs or a seasoned skier chasing fresh powder and steeps, the variety of terrain, well-maintained conditions, and laid-back vibe deliver exactly what you need.

2026–27 season (projected): opens Dec 5, 2026; daily skiing from Dec 12; night skiing from Dec 26; closes Mar 22, 2027.

Hours: Sun 9am–4:30pm; Mon–Tue 10am–4:30pm; Wed–Sat and holidays 9am–9pm (once night skiing begins).

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/ski/ | Hours of operation

items.title: Nordic Skiing
items.html:
Few activities capture the quiet beauty of northern Michigan in winter quite like Nordic skiing. At Shanty Creek Resort, you’ll find 9.5 km of groomed, track-set cross-country trails that wind between the resort’s villages for a scenic, heart-healthy village-to-village skiing experience.

Multi-purpose trail: If Nordic skiing isn’t your thing, a 3 km groomed trail in Schuss Village is set aside for fat tire biking and snowshoeing.

Nordic Center: Classic and skate ski rentals and snowshoe rentals. Day trail pass $22 adult / $14 child; ski packages $34 adult; snowshoes $28.

Hours (2026–27, projected Dec 26 – Mar 13): Thu & Mon 9am–4pm; Fri 10am–4pm; Sat, Sun & holidays 9am–5pm; closed Tue & Wed.

Lessons: Book 48 hours ahead. Cancellations need 48 hours’ notice for a refund. Requests for a specific instructor need at least 3 days’ notice.

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/ski/nordic-trails/

items.title: Alpine Tubing
items.html:
If skiing and snowboarding aren’t your thing, there’s still a fast and fun way to enjoy the snow. Alpine Tubing at Summit Mountain is a must-try winter activity, with all the thrills of sledding and none of the uphill climb.

You’ll hear laughter echoing across the slopes as guests of all ages race down the tubing lanes and ride the surface lift back to the top. No skills required. Just hold on and enjoy the ride!

What to know:

  • Sessions start at the top of every hour
  • $30 per hour
  • Online booking only
  • Participants must be 36″ tall

Hours (2026–27, projected Dec 19 – Mar 14): Fri 4pm–10pm; Sat & holidays 10am–10pm; Sun & holiday Mondays 10am–4pm.

Parents note: The last two hours on Friday and Saturday nights are recommended for adults only.

More info & booking: https://www.shantycreek.com/ski/more-on-the-snow/#tubing

items.title: Fat Tire Biking
items.html:
Ride on, even in the snow

Try fat tire biking on the groomed 3 km multi-purpose trail at Schuss Village. Whether you're an experienced rider or just looking to try something new, this packed trail offers a smooth, scenic ride through snow-covered landscapes. It’s shared with snowshoers.

Don’t have your own bike? Fat tire bike rentals are available from Paddles & Pedals, 206 N. Bridge St. in downtown Bellaire. Call 231-533-4449 to reserve and confirm winter availability.

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/ski/nordic-trails/

items.title: Snow Glide Tours
items.html:
Experience winter like never before with Shanty Creek’s Snow Glide Tours, a scenic, cozy, and memorable ride for all ages.

Tours depart from The Lakeview Hotel's front circle. Each 45-minute guided ride winds through the snow-blanketed landscapes of Summit Village, with sweeping views and no effort required.

Each tour seats up to 9 passengers and is pulled behind “Big Blue,” a double-track snowmobile. The Snow Glide has seatbelts, and passengers must be able to sit independently while buckled.

Schedule (last season): on the hour, 10am–3pm, on Saturdays, Sundays, and select holiday dates. The 2026–27 schedule had not been posted as of Oct 2026.

Price: $29 per seat
Seating is limited, so book early. Questions: 231-533-3000.

More info & booking: https://www.shantycreek.com/snow-glide-tours/

items.title: Snowshoeing
items.html:
Forge Your Own Trail – Adventure Awaits

Whether you're a seasoned snowshoer or trying it for the first time, snowshoeing at Shanty Creek offers a peaceful and scenic way to explore the winter woods of northern Michigan.

Slip on a pair and start walking—no special skills required. You can blaze your own path through the snowy landscape or follow the groomed 3km multi-purpose trail located at Schuss Village, shared with fat tire bikers and designed to minimize trail damage while keeping everyone safe.

Rental Equipment is available at the Nordic Center in Schuss Village, including snowshoes and poles.

This is a perfect winter activity for those seeking quiet beauty, fresh air, and an easy-going workout.

More Info: https://www.shantycreek.com/ski/more-on-the-snow/

items.title: Cedar River
items.html:
“...a pleasure to play and a beauty to experience.” Cedar River’s glacial-carved canvas was perfect for famed course architect Tom Weiskopf to design this masterpiece.

Among "America’s Top 100 Resort Courses" in Golf Week and the “Top 1,000 Courses in the World” by Rolex. Along with The Legend, Cedar River is listed among Michigan’s Top 20 Public Courses according to Golf Magazine.

Cedar River Scorecard

Cedar River Tee Times or call 231-533-2020

Closed Mondays and Tuesdays

items.title: Foot & Disc Golf
items.html:
Mix the skills of soccer or disc golf with the scoring of golf, and you get a fun new way to bring the whole family to the links. Shanty Creek has an exclusive 9-hole Foot & Disc Golf course with hybrid basket cups. The goal, like golf, is the fewest shots from tee to hole.

Ready to play? $12 includes a ball or disc. To make a tee time, call 231-533-2020.

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/golf/golf-2-0/#footgolf

items.title: Hawk's Eye
items.html:
“...the perfect complement to Cedar River and The Legend.”

Adding to Shanty Creek's golf reputation, this John Robinson design features incredible vistas, water hazards on 9 of 18 holes, and putting greens to challenge golfers of all levels. Named among "Michigan's Top Courses" from Golf Advisor and the “Top 25 Course Layouts in the US."

Hawk's Eye Scorecard

Hawk's Eye Tee Times or call 231-533-2020

Closed Mondays and Tuesdays

items.title: Schuss Mountain
items.html:
Schuss Mtn delivers a challenge for even the most accomplished golfers. Par eludes many throughout 7,013 yards of pine-dotted forests, wetlands, and rolling hills.

Playing like two distinct 9-hole courses, the front doglegs through pine forests on a flat pitch. Then on the back, play jumps up and down the rolling hills of Antrim County delivering an overall exciting golf experience made only better by our crew's tremendous care to its course conditions.

Schuss Mountain Scorecard

Schuss Mountain Tee Times or call 231-533-2020

Closed Mondays and Tuesdays

items.title: Summit
items.html:
“...an under-appreciated gem.” While length is not a factor, Summit forces accomplished golfers to test their short game. Precise landings and fast, challenging greens will make you earn your score.

A Par Three tee box on every hole gives junior golfers a fun (and less intimidating!) way to develop their game.

Summit Scorecard

Summit Tee Times or call 231-533-2020

Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays

items.title: The Legend
items.html:
by Arnold Palmer

The Legend's reputation has been built on multiple elevation changes, doglegs, water hazards, and well-placed traps. Its setting includes views of Lake Bellaire and the actual Shanty Creek trickles through your round.

Arnold Palmer helped introduce northern Michigan golf to the world when Golf Magazine named it among the “Top Resort Courses” in the US. 4½ stars from Golf Digest.

The Legend Scorecard

The Legend Tee Times or call 231-533-2020

Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays

items.title: Beach Club – Lake Bellaire (Private Access)
items.html:
Designed exclusively for resort guests, Shanty Creek’s private Beach Club sits on the shores of beautiful Lake Bellaire, offering around 200 feet of sandy shoreline and a serene swim area that’s ideal for families and couples alike.

What You’ll Find
  • Sandy beach & loungers for sunbathing and relaxation
  • Designated swim zone for safe, shallow water play
  • Kayak and paddleboard rentals available nearby
  • Easy access to restrooms and picnic facilities, plus grill areas
  • Perfect proximity to nearby resort amenities—dining, tennis, fitness & entertainment are all just a short walk away
Location
  • Situated on Lake Bellaire, just a few minutes from Summit Village
  • Close to dining and shopping options, including Short’s Brewing in downtown Bellaire (~3 minutes away)
Why You’ll Love It
  • A private, peaceful escape with crystal-clear waters and shimmering lake views
  • Buffer from crowds → relaxing space for unwinding
  • Splendid sunsets and water views — perfect for low-key evenings

Access: Only available to registered Shanty Creek lodging guests.
More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/

items.title: The Lakeview Hotel
items.html:
Enjoy the heart of Summit Village at the Lakeview Hotel, perched above Lake Bellaire with views for miles. Even if you're not staying at the hotel, it's the resort's hub for dining, pools, and events.

Dining

  • The Lakeview – bar and grill fare with sunset views over Lake Bellaire. Breakfast daily 7–11am; lunch daily 11:30am–4pm; dinner Sun–Thu 5–9pm, Fri–Sat 5–10pm; bar opens daily at 11:30am; happy hour daily 5–6:30pm.
  • CoffeeBAR (proudly serving Starbucks) – in the Great Room lobby. Sun–Thu 7am–2pm, Fri–Sat 7am–6pm.

Pools

  • Your pool pass covers the Lakeview indoor pool (open daily 9am–11pm) and the seasonal outdoor pool. Bring the towels we provide with your pool pass (the resort does not supply them).

Nearby in Summit Village

  • Tennis courts, the children's playground, and The Legend and Summit golf courses
  • Alpine tubing and Snow Glide Tours in winter

Address: 5780 Shanty Creek Road, Bellaire, MI 49615
Phone: 231-533-3000

More info: https://www.shantycreek.com/stay/dining/
